title: Hadith Knowledge
description: Little Muslim → Mid. Short questions for children who know the first hadith basics. Covers transmission, careful reporting, good character, sincere care, preventing wrongdoing, supporting the sick, hospitality, privacy, forgiveness, familiar manners, balanced practice, clear teaching and learning through questions. Includes everyday home and classroom situations. An adult may read questions aloud or explain unfamiliar words. All questions are Mid level within the Kids audience.
levelMethod: Mid describes the knowledge and understanding needed across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Builds on first hadith basics through simple meanings, common misconceptions and straightforward applications. No narrator biographies, chain analysis, specialist grading debates or memorization of reference numbers is required. Level is editorial guidance, not calibrated with children's reading or response data. Quiz performance describes learning needs, not a child's faith or worth.

review.referenceCheck: Linked hadith reports and the hadith introduction checked during preparation. The Sunan Abi Dawud 4990 report is graded Hasan by Al-Albani on the linked source; most other reports are from Sahih al-Bukhari or Sahih Muslim. Sahih Muslim 5 is in the collection's Introduction. Questions and explanations are original child-friendly educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Present-day scenarios illustrate applications; they are not events narrated in the cited reports. A child's duty is not equated with an adult's legal responsibility. General teachings about avoiding harm and caring for others are not permission to mistreat anyone of another faith. Reporting concerns to trusted adults is distinguished from spreading unverified claims. Forgiveness does not require tolerating ongoing harm; preventing bullying does not require a child to use physical force. Visitors, permission, gifts and learning routines are presented with suitable adult guidance. The right-side example concerns putting on shoes and does not generalize every action or judge disability. Breathing guidance concerns the vessel, not restricting normal breathing. Repetition in teaching is explained by its purpose of understanding, not as a requirement to repeat every sentence in ordinary speech. No question asks children to judge another person's faith or worth. This is not independent scholarly approval or a completed review with children.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: How have hadith reports reached later generations?

options.text: Through people transmitting them and scholars preserving them
Through choosing the most popular guesses
Through inventing a new message each year
Through treating every poem as the Prophet's ﷺ words

questions.explanation: Hadith reports were transmitted and carefully studied. Learning about that process helps us appreciate why reliable reporting matters.

questions.question: What does the hadith about repeating everything we hear warn against?

options.text: Checking whether a story is reliable
Passing on reports without proper care
Asking a teacher to clarify something
Admitting that we do not know

questions.explanation: Repeating everything we hear can spread falsehood. We should be careful about what we present as true.

questions.question: Which conduct does the hadith about a Muslim's tongue and hands praise?

options.text: Hurting people whenever we feel annoyed
Using insults to win attention
Keeping fellow Muslims safe from our harmful words and actions
Pushing others to prove our importance

questions.explanation: The hadith connects good Muslim conduct with avoiding harm through words and hands. It calls us to take our behavior seriously.

questions.question: How did the Prophet ﷺ explain helping someone who is wronging others?

options.text: Help them hurt more people
Hide every wrong they commit
Praise them for being powerful
Stop them from doing the wrong

questions.explanation: Stopping someone from oppressing others is a way of helping them. Supporting a person does not mean supporting their harmful behavior.

questions.question: Which quality did the Prophet ﷺ praise in the hadith about the best among people?

options.text: Good manners and character
Owning the most expensive clothes
Always being the loudest speaker
Making others feel small

questions.explanation: The hadith gives special value to good character. What we learn should influence how we speak and treat people.

questions.question: What attitude toward fellow Muslims fits the hadith about sincere care and advice?

options.text: Enjoying their embarrassment
Wanting what is truly good for them
Pretending to help while planning harm
Giving advice only to show off

questions.explanation: The hadith teaches sincerity, including toward fellow Muslims. Helpful advice should come from care, not a wish to humiliate.

questions.question: Which act of care is explicitly encouraged in the hadith about people who are ill?

options.text: Mocking someone for being unwell
Making illness into a reason for exclusion
Visiting the sick
Ignoring every person who needs care

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ encouraged visiting the sick. This teaching reminds us to care about people when they are unwell.

questions.question: Which pair of actions did the Prophet ﷺ praise when asked about good Islamic conduct?

options.text: Boasting about wealth and refusing every greeting
Keeping all food and mocking newcomers
Speaking only to people who can give us gifts
Feeding others and offering greetings of peace

questions.explanation: The report joins feeding others with giving salam. Kindness and a welcoming greeting are part of everyday Islamic conduct.

questions.question: Which attitude does the hadith warn us to avoid toward fellow Muslims?

options.text: Envy and hostility
Wishing them well
Treating them with respect
Caring about their dignity

questions.explanation: The hadith warns against envy and hostility. Another person's blessing should not become a reason to hate or mistreat them.

questions.question: What does the hadith teach a guest to avoid?

options.text: Respecting the host's situation
Staying in a way that burdens the host
Being grateful for hospitality
Speaking politely during a visit

questions.explanation: The hadith teaches generous hospitality and consideration from guests. Visiting should not become a burden on the host.

questions.question: What does the hadith teach after asking permission to enter three times without receiving it?

options.text: Keep demanding entry without stopping
Push the door open
Return rather than force entry
Assume silence means permission

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught returning when permission is not given after three requests. Respecting another person's home includes accepting that limit.

questions.question: When three people sit together, what private conversation does the hadith warn against?

options.text: All three joining a friendly conversation
One person asking a question everyone can hear
Listening respectfully when someone is speaking
Two speaking secretly while leaving the third excluded

questions.explanation: The hadith considers the hurt caused by excluding the third person. Conversation should take other people's feelings into account.

questions.question: What does the hadith teach about forgiving another person?

options.text: Allah increases a person's honor through forgiveness
Forgiveness always makes a person worthless
Only revenge can bring honor
Forgiving means losing every right to safety

questions.explanation: The hadith praises forgiveness as a source of honor from Allah. Forgiveness need not be confused with worthlessness or weakness.

questions.question: When putting on shoes, which side did the Prophet ﷺ like to begin with?

options.text: The left
The right
Whichever shoe was more expensive
A different side for each new day

questions.explanation: Aishah described the Prophet ﷺ liking to begin with the right when putting on shoes. This is a familiar example of everyday Sunnah.

questions.question: What does the hadith teach about breathing while drinking?

options.text: Always breathe directly into the cup
Blow into another person's drink for fun
Do not breathe into the drinking vessel
Treat drinking manners as having no guidance

questions.explanation: The hadith teaches not breathing into the vessel. We can move the cup away when we need to breathe.

questions.question: What does the hadith about ease in religion warn against?

options.text: Learning at a sensible pace
Taking guidance when we need it
Trying to improve steadily
Overburdening ourselves until we cannot continue

questions.explanation: The hadith teaches balance rather than making religion unnecessarily difficult. A manageable approach helps us continue learning and practicing.

questions.question: Why did the Prophet ﷺ repeat a statement three times in the report narrated by Anas?

options.text: So listeners could understand it properly
So nobody could ask a question
So the message would become a different teaching
So only the fastest listeners could learn

questions.explanation: The report connects repetition with understanding. Teaching should help people grasp the message rather than leave them confused.

questions.question: How did the Prophet ﷺ respond when a visitor wanted to ask him questions about religion?

options.text: He said learning through questions was always forbidden
He allowed the visitor to ask
He refused every question about prayer
He demanded that the visitor already know every answer

questions.explanation: The report shows a visitor asking questions and receiving answers. Asking to understand can be part of sincere learning.

questions.question: What does the hadith warn against when trying to make people laugh?

options.text: Speaking truthfully and kindly
Enjoying a truthful funny memory
Telling lies for their amusement
Avoiding jokes that deceive people

questions.explanation: The report warns against lying to entertain people. Getting a laugh does not make deliberate falsehood acceptable.

questions.question: What can count as charity when a Muslim plants a tree or sows seeds?

options.text: Keeping every living creature away forever
Boasting that nobody else deserves food
Destroying the crop just for attention
A person, bird or animal eating from it

questions.explanation: The hadith counts others eating from a Muslim's planting as charity. Useful plants can benefit people and animals.

questions.question: Are preserving hadith reports and inventing new sayings for the Prophet ﷺ the same thing?

options.text: No, preservation passes on reports rather than inventing them
Yes, both mean making up whatever sounds nice
Yes, a scholar must invent a new Prophet's saying yearly
No, because no hadith reports have ever been preserved

questions.explanation: Scholars preserve and study transmitted reports. That work is different from inventing a saying and attributing it to the Prophet ﷺ.

questions.question: Does hearing a story from many people automatically prove it true?

options.text: Yes, every repeated story must be true
No, repetition is not the same as reliable evidence
Yes, the most exciting version is always correct
No, because checking reports is never useful

questions.explanation: A story can spread widely without becoming true. The warning against repeating everything we hear encourages care before passing information on.

questions.question: If we do not hit people but keep insulting them, have we followed the whole lesson about tongue and hands?

options.text: Yes, insults never count as harm
Yes, words have no effect on anyone
No, harmful speech matters too
No, because the hadith encourages pushing instead

questions.explanation: The teaching includes speech as well as physical action. Avoiding one kind of harm does not make another kind acceptable.

questions.question: Does helping a friend mean joining them when they bully someone?

options.text: Yes, friendship makes every action right
Yes, only the strongest child's feelings matter
No, because helping anyone is always forbidden
No, help them stop the wrongdoing

questions.explanation: Refusing to support bullying can help both the victim and the friend doing wrong. Seek a trusted adult's help when needed.

questions.question: Does knowing many religious facts replace the need for good manners?

options.text: No, good character still matters
Yes, knowledge gives permission to insult
Yes, manners matter only for new learners
No, because learning facts is always wrong

questions.explanation: The hadith praises good character. Knowledge should help us improve our behavior, not become an excuse for treating people badly.

questions.question: Which purpose best fits sincere advice to someone learning?

options.text: Make the whole class laugh at them
Help them understand and improve
Prove that they have no value
Collect praise by exposing their mistakes

questions.explanation: Sincere advice seeks the other person's good. Showing off or humiliating a learner misses that purpose.

questions.question: Does caring for someone who is ill mean ignoring instructions meant to protect them and visitors?

options.text: Yes, concern means visiting however we want
Yes, the person must accept visitors at every moment
No, care should respect suitable arrangements
No, because the sick never deserve companionship

questions.explanation: The teaching encourages care, not inconsiderate visiting. Let an adult arrange an appropriate way to support someone who is unwell.

questions.question: Does the hadith limit greetings of peace only to our closest friends?

options.text: Yes, only our best friend deserves a greeting
Yes, only people who bring gifts may be greeted
No, because it forbids all greetings
No, it mentions people we know and do not know

questions.explanation: The hadith encourages a welcoming salam beyond a narrow circle of friends. Children can follow it in appropriate settings with adult guidance.

questions.question: Can we work to improve without wishing another person would lose their blessing?

options.text: Yes, learning and wishing others well can go together
No, improvement always requires hating someone else's success
Yes, but only if we secretly hope they fail
No, because envy is the only useful motivation

questions.explanation: Avoiding envy does not mean giving up our own efforts. We can seek good for ourselves without resenting someone else's blessing.

questions.question: Does generous hospitality give guests permission to ignore the host's needs?

options.text: Yes, the host's situation never matters
No, guests should be considerate too
Yes, guests may demand anything they imagine
No, because welcoming guests is always wrong

questions.explanation: Hospitality and consideration belong together. A guest should appreciate kindness without turning the visit into hardship for the host.

questions.question: If permission is not given, does asking three times allow us to enter anyway?

options.text: Yes, three requests make any home ours
Yes, an unanswered request is always permission
No, the teaching is to return
No, but we should damage the door instead

questions.explanation: Asking is not the same as receiving permission. The hadith tells us to return rather than insist on entering.

questions.question: Why can secret talk between two of three people be hurtful?

options.text: It always makes the third person feel welcome
It proves the third person's feelings do not matter
It makes every private conversation harmless
It can leave the third person feeling excluded

questions.explanation: The report explains the concern as causing sadness. This lesson encourages consideration, rather than a ban on every kind of privacy.

questions.question: Does forgiving an ordinary mistake mean a person has no dignity?

options.text: No, the hadith connects forgiveness with increased honor
Yes, dignity belongs only to people who take revenge
Yes, forgiveness makes kindness meaningless
No, but it requires allowing harm to continue

questions.explanation: The hadith praises forgiveness. It does not require remaining in an unsafe situation or refusing help when harm continues.

questions.question: What does the report about beginning with the right when putting on shoes illustrate?

options.text: Only expensive shoes can be worn respectfully
Sunnah includes familiar everyday habits
Every ordinary habit is too small to learn about
People with different physical abilities deserve mockery

questions.explanation: The report shows guidance in an ordinary routine. Learning it should encourage care, not ridicule toward someone with different needs or abilities.

questions.question: Does avoiding breathing into a cup mean we should avoid taking normal breaths?

options.text: Yes, drinking requires stopping normal breathing
Yes, breathing is always bad manners
No, move the cup away to breathe
No, but we should breathe into someone else's cup

questions.explanation: The instruction concerns breathing into the vessel. Moving it away lets us breathe normally while observing the taught manner.

questions.question: Does avoiding unnecessary religious hardship mean abandoning every good practice?

options.text: Yes, learning and worship must both stop
Yes, any effort is automatically wrong
No, because only exhaustion proves sincerity
No, aim for a sound and manageable approach

questions.explanation: The hadith encourages a balanced approach that can continue. Avoiding overburdening is different from rejecting learning and good practice.

questions.question: What is the important purpose of repetition in this teaching report?

options.text: Helping the listener understand
Making learning feel impossible
Replacing the original teaching with a new invention
Showing that slower learners deserve ridicule

questions.explanation: Repetition is used to make meaning clearer. Its purpose is understanding, not embarrassing someone who needs more time.

questions.question: Does asking a respectful question to understand a lesson prove that learning is unimportant to us?

options.text: Yes, every question means rejecting the lesson
No, questions can show a wish to understand
Yes, only people who know nothing ever ask
No, because answers should always be invented

questions.explanation: The visitor's questions helped clarify religious teachings. Asking sincerely can support learning rather than oppose it.

questions.question: Does getting a laugh make a deliberately false report true?

options.text: Yes, enough laughter makes every claim accurate
Yes, jokes remove every need for honesty
No, laughter does not change falsehood into truth
No, because kind truthful humor is always forbidden

questions.explanation: The warning concerns lying to make people laugh. Enjoyment is not a reason to present a deliberate falsehood as a fact.

questions.question: Does the planting hadith mention benefit only when a human eats from the crop?

options.text: Yes, birds and animals can never benefit
Yes, only the planter may ever eat from it
No, because the hadith says planting has no value
No, birds and animals are mentioned too

questions.explanation: The hadith mentions people, birds and animals eating from the planting. Its benefit can reach several kinds of living creatures.

questions.question: Your lesson says a hadith was transmitted by narrators and preserved in a collection. What does this describe?

options.text: How a report was passed on and recorded
How to invent a new saying for the Prophet ﷺ
How to choose a report by counting likes
How to turn any poem into Quran

questions.explanation: Transmission and collection concern passing on and preserving reports. They do not give permission to invent words for the Prophet ﷺ.

questions.question: A group chat shares an unchecked story about a classmate. Which response follows the warning about repeating everything we hear?

options.text: Forward it before anyone else can
Do not forward it as fact; ask an adult to help check
Add details to make the story more exciting
Assume every message must be accurate

questions.explanation: Unverified repetition can spread falsehood and hurt someone. Pause rather than passing it on as a fact.

questions.question: You feel annoyed during a game. Which choice follows the hadith about avoiding harm through tongue and hands?

options.text: Insult a classmate because you did not hit them
Push someone because you stayed silent
Speak respectfully and keep your hands from hurting others
Use words and hands to frighten the other team

questions.explanation: The teaching includes both speech and physical conduct. Feeling annoyed does not give permission to harm other players.

questions.question: A friend asks you to help bully a smaller child. What is real help for your friend?

options.text: Join in to prove loyalty
Hide the bullying from every adult
Encourage your friend to become crueler
Refuse and get a teacher's help to stop the bullying

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ explained helping a wrongdoer as stopping their wrongdoing. A teacher can help protect the child and address the bullying safely.

questions.question: Hasan scores well in a quiz but mocks slower learners. Which reminder fits the hadith about good character?

options.text: Knowledge should go with respectful manners
High scores give permission to humiliate others
Only slower learners need to practice kindness
Quiz winners are allowed to ignore everyone's feelings

questions.explanation: The hadith praises good character. Learning should help Hasan become considerate, not give him a reason to look down on others.

questions.question: A friend misunderstands a lesson and asks for help. Which response shows sincere care?

options.text: Use their mistake to embarrass them
Explain kindly and ask the teacher if unsure
Pretend to help while teaching something false
Insist that needing help makes them worthless

questions.explanation: Sincere care aims at another person's good. Be kind, and get suitable help rather than inventing an answer.

questions.question: A relative is unwell. What is an appropriate way for a child to practice care?

options.text: Demand a visit even if the family says rest is needed
Make fun of the person's illness
Ask a parent about a suitable visit or message
Tell others the person deserves to be ignored

questions.explanation: The hadith encourages caring for the sick. A parent can help choose a thoughtful way to show support.

questions.question: At a family gathering, which pair of actions follows the report about food and salam?

options.text: Hide the food and refuse every greeting
Speak only to people who give presents
Mock guests who are new to you
Help serve permitted food and greet people respectfully

questions.explanation: The report praises feeding others and giving salam. At a family gathering, a child can practice both with adult guidance.

questions.question: Your friend receives a learning award you hoped for. Which response avoids envy?

options.text: Congratulate them and keep working on your own learning
Wish they would lose every good thing
Damage the award to make yourself feel better
Treat their success as a reason to hate them

questions.explanation: Another person's success need not become a reason for resentment. You can wish them well and still improve your own learning.

questions.question: You visit a friend with your parent, and the host needs to rest. What shows consideration?

options.text: Insist that guests may stay as long as they want
Follow your parent's guidance and leave politely when appropriate
Demand that the host ignore their own needs
Mock the host for needing a break

questions.explanation: A considerate guest respects the host's situation. Follow the adults' arrangements without turning hospitality into a burden.

questions.question: With your parent, you have asked permission to enter three times without being invited. What should you do?

options.text: Push the door open because you waited
Keep knocking to force an answer
Stay with your parent and leave respectfully
Enter through another opening without permission

questions.explanation: The hadith teaches returning when permission is not given after three requests. Respect the family's privacy and follow your parent's guidance.

questions.question: Three classmates sit together. Two begin whispering while deliberately leaving the third out. Which choice follows the hadith's lesson?

options.text: Keep whispering to make the child feel unwanted
Laugh whenever the child asks to join
Tell the child their feelings never matter
Include the third child in the shared conversation

questions.explanation: The hadith takes the excluded person's sadness seriously. A shared conversation can help everyone feel included.

questions.question: A friend makes an ordinary mistake and sincerely apologizes. What follows the hadith's praise of forgiveness?

options.text: Consider forgiving without trying to humiliate them
Insist that only revenge can protect your dignity
Use the mistake to shame them every day
Tell them forgiveness is always worthless

questions.explanation: Forgiveness can be honorable. You may explain your feelings and seek repair without making humiliation your goal.

questions.question: You are able to put on your own shoes and want to follow the reported Sunnah. Which shoe do you begin with?

options.text: The left shoe
The right shoe
Whichever shoe is more expensive
A different shoe according to a daily guessing game

questions.explanation: Aishah's report mentions beginning with the right when putting on shoes. Follow the habit as you are able, without judging other people's circumstances.

questions.question: While drinking, you need to take a breath. What follows the hadith's teaching about the vessel?

options.text: Breathe directly into the drink
Blow into your friend's cup instead
Move the cup away before breathing
Assume breathing into the cup is required

questions.explanation: The teaching is not to breathe into the drinking vessel. Moving the cup away lets you take a normal breath.

questions.question: A child adds so many extra practices that they cannot keep up. Which plan reflects the hadith's guidance?

options.text: Keep adding more only to appear impressive
Assume tiredness always proves a better faith
Give up every useful lesson forever
Ask a parent or teacher for a balanced, suitable routine

questions.explanation: The hadith warns against overburdening. Children can learn and practice with adult guidance at a suitable, steady pace.

questions.question: A younger learner asks you to repeat a checked teaching. Which response reflects the purpose of the Prophet's ﷺ repetition?

options.text: Repeat it patiently so they can understand
Mock them for not catching it immediately
Change the teaching to make it exciting
Refuse because only fast learners deserve help

questions.explanation: The report connects repetition with understanding. Repeat carefully and patiently instead of shaming someone who needs to hear it again.

questions.question: You do not understand a hadith explanation. What is a helpful next step?

options.text: Pretend to understand and invent the meaning
Ask your teacher a respectful question
Mock anyone else who asks for clarification
Decide that sincere questions are always forbidden

questions.explanation: The report shows questions being answered as part of learning. A respectful question can help you understand instead of guessing.

questions.question: A friend wants you to tell a false story as a real event to make everyone laugh. What should you choose?

options.text: Tell it as fact because laughter makes lying right
Blame another child when the lie is discovered
Refuse to deceive and choose truthful, kind humor
Add a fake hadith to make it sound convincing

questions.explanation: The warning is against lying for amusement. Choose humor that does not depend on presenting false claims as true.

questions.question: With your teacher, you help grow a fruit plant from which people or birds may eat. Which teaching fits?

options.text: Only cash can ever count as charity
Birds benefiting from plants can never matter
Planting is valuable only when everyone praises the planter
Useful planting can become a source of charity

questions.explanation: The hadith describes charity through people or animals eating from a Muslim's planting. A supervised gardening activity can help you understand that benefit.
